newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul drafts 30.6 trilion won "anti-disaster" plan.
newsitem.headline: Seoul drafts 30.6 trilion won "anti-disaster" plan.

text.p: South Korea on Saturday unveiled a draft plan requiring an investment of 30.6 trillion won over the next five years to help prevent and cope with natural disasters.
The home ministry said in a statement that the draft plan, adopted at a meeting of vice ministers, would be finalised after cabinet approval.

During the 1997-2001 period, seven new dams will be built at an investment of 1.71 trillion won and various river improvement projects will be undertaken with an investment of 3.51 trillion won, the statement said.
About nine trillion won will be required to improve anti-drought facilities in areas which have been suffering from chronic shortages of drinking and farming water, the statement said.
The statement said the government plans to strengthen the nation's overall capability to better counter earthquakes.
South Korea is regarded as relatively safe from earthquakes, but recent studies have shown a possibility of strong earthquakes occurring on the Korean peninsula within 2010, the statement said.
